name: Tinkerers Who Changed the World
description: From a Han court official and a Mainz goldsmith to Edison, Tesla and the Wrights: the inventors who gave us paper, print, light, the phone, the car and flight.

checkpoints.name: Paper, gears and type
checkpoints.note: Cai Lun is credited with improving paper at the Han court, and al-Jazari wrote a book on ingenious water machines and clocks. In the mid-1400s Johannes Gutenberg set up his printing press in Mainz, and books began to multiply.

checkpoints.name: Steam, springs and sparks
checkpoints.note: The steam engine, improved by James Watt, drove new machines, and Richard Arkwright's mills brought factory spinning. John Harrison built clocks that kept time at sea, Alessandro Volta's voltaic pile gave steady current, and George Stephenson turned engines into locomotives.

checkpoints.name: Wires, pictures and bangs
checkpoints.note: Louis Braille's raised dots opened reading to blind people, while Samuel Morse sent messages by wire. Louis Daguerre fixed images on metal plates, Isambard Kingdom Brunel built railways and ships, and Alfred Nobel patented dynamite.

checkpoints.name: Light, voice and power
checkpoints.note: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone, and Thomas Edison's incandescent light bulb brought electric light to homes. Karl Benz built a petrol car, Nikola Tesla championed alternating current, Gustave Eiffel raised his tower, and Guglielmo Marconi and the Lumiere brothers showed wireless and film.

checkpoints.name: Flight, code and web
checkpoints.note: The Wright brothers flew the Wright Flyer in 1903. Later, Konrad Zuse built early programmable computers in Germany, Stephanie Kwolek discovered the fibre behind Kevlar, and Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web.
